summary: Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2004. She studied under Michael Witzel, Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, Kausalya Hart, Shaligram Shukla, Saudamani Deshmukh, James W. Benson, and Thomas Burke.

Susan L. Beningson works in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University, attested in 2009, under the doctoral supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr.

Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from UCLA (circa 1968–1972). She spent her career at Ohio State University as Professor (circa 1971–2000) and later Distinguished University Professor, Emerita.
Susan Meinheit is a Tibetology scholar whose career includes posts at the Library of Congress, attested in 1998 and 2007.

Susan Naquin, a scholar of Sinology and history, earned her BA at Stanford and MA and PhD at Yale. She served as assistant professor of history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and as professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard (PhD 1977–1986) and Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and became Director of the Einstein Forum in 2000.
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who held a post in the religion department at Amherst College from circa 1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing her PhD at SOAS in 1995, she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and became Professor at UEA.

Susannah Deane is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Bangor, Bristol, and Cardiff (PhD 2010–2015). Her posts include British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Bristol (2017–2021) and bid writer at the University of the West of England (2023).

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Sarah Lawrence, Radcliffe, and Harvard (PhD circa 1953–1955). She taught political science at Harvard (circa 1955–1963) and became a professor at the University of Chicago in 1964.
Susanne Kerekes is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Trinity College, Hartford.

Susanne Mrozik is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Harvard under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. She held posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Visva-Bharati University. Sen later held lecturer posts at Visva-Bharati University in 1986 and at the University of Birmingham in the Department of Theology.

Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) was an Indologist educated at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, SOAS (D.Litt.), and University of Bonn. He taught at Presidency, Calcutta, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Dhaka (circa 1923–1947).
Susmita Basu Majumdar is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, where she held an academic post circa 2004.

Susumu Kajiura is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post as research assistant at Kyoto University in 1999 and served as head of humanities research at the Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property (attested 2001).

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Makio Takemura at the University of Tsukuba (circa 1993–2003). He held part-time lecturing posts at Hanazono University, Kyoto University, and Bukkyo University.

Susumu Shimazono is a religious studies and Japanology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013) and held professorial and director roles at Sophia University from circa 2013.

Susumu Winston Nakamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Japanology. He completed an MA at UC Berkeley under Ferdinand Lessing (circa 1935–1939) and worked as a lecturer at UC Boulder (circa 1942–1946) and UC Berkeley (circa 1946–1973).

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Otani, Paris, and Kyoto, he studied under Gessho Sasaki, Enga Teramoto, Sylvain Lévi, and Louis de La Vallée Poussin, and was long-term professor at Otani University.
